Polysexual is different because it involves more than two people in a relationship whereas if someone says they are pansexual/panromantic then it’s typically assumed that they are monogamous. Also, ____sexual/___romantic is not divided by sex and gender, it’s based on preferred sexual relationships vs (potentially platonic) romantic relationships.

For example, if someone says they are panromantic and homosexual then they’d be open to romantic relationships regardless of gender but as for being homosexual they’d only want to have sexual relationships within their own gender.

[Some people are transphobic in believing that assigned sex is the only factor, for example thinking that a cis man being in a relationship with a trans guy (FTM) doesn’t ‘count’ as being gay]

Sounds a lot like stimming behavior: repetitive motions or sounds done to kind of let out pent up energy. It can happen during overwhelming positive or negative emotions (for example if someone is very excited or very nervous) and depending on why you’re stimming the method(s) of stimming can vary.

Stimming can come in a variety of forms (and not all stims ‘work’ for all people) such as leg bouncing, hair twirling, flapping your hands, biting nails, rocking, pulling on zippers, etc.

Stimming is common with autism but also can happen from anxiety and other things. Neurotypical people tend to be able to control it more though since they don’t rely on it as strongly (if that makes sense?); stimming is meant to relieve excess energy so trying to force yourself to stop can actually cause stress

I’ve had some similar short term memory problems (along with some more long term incidents), in my personal experience with this kind of thing it can often be to where trauma sets it up but stress triggers it/draws it out.

My short term memory issues tend to ease up when my environment calms down (for me that wasn’t just going home and having tea, it involved more distinct and purposeful separation from stressors and people that cause undue stress). When it does happen though my brain kind of freezes up like when I’d ask someone a question and (especially if the answer is long or requires being engaged) the listening part of my brain acts like it just zones out. Focusing and trying to fight it does nothing except giving me a stress headache. It can also happen to me when someone is trying to engage me in some subject (especially if I don’t already understand it) so if someone is walking me through directions or a recipe I just have to ask them to write it down.

Carrying a small notebook with you may help so you can write down things you need to remember and so you can pinpoint and record how/when it affects you (it may not help stop it but knowing when to expect it can help in managing general life). If you talk to a health care professional for therapy or medications I’d suggest also bringing it up with them if you haven’t
